title: Preparation of potassium dichromate from chromite ore
body: Potassium dichromate is made from chromite ore, FeCr2O4. The ore is fused with sodium carbonate in free access of air: 4 FeCr2O4 + 8 Na2CO3 + 7 O2 -> 8 Na2CrO4 + 2 Fe2O3 + 8 CO2. The yellow solution of sodium chromate is filtered and acidified with sulphuric acid, and orange sodium dichromate, Na2Cr2O7.2H2O, crystallises: 2 Na2CrO4 + 2 H+ -> Na2Cr2O7 + 2 Na+ + H2O. Because sodium dichromate is more soluble than potassium dichromate, it is treated with potassium chloride, and orange crystals of K2Cr2O7 separate: Na2Cr2O7 + 2 KCl -> K2Cr2O7 + 2 NaCl. In aqueous solution chromate and dichromate interconvert depending on pH: 2 CrO4(2-) + 2 H+ -> Cr2O7(2-) + H2O, and Cr2O7(2-) + 2 OH- -> 2 CrO4(2-) + H2O. The chromate ion is tetrahedral, while the dichromate ion is two tetrahedra sharing one corner, with a Cr-O-Cr angle of 126 degrees.
